meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Fri 27 Nov: NIFTY 50 rises 0.25% to 25,884.50; Nifty IT up 3.66%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 0.25% to 25,884.50 and the Sensex 0.46% to 84,328.59 on Thursday 26 Nov, after giving back part of an early rise; Nifty Bank fell 0.26% to 63,535.30 (Angel One, India TV, Liquide).
Nifty IT rose 3.66% and Nifty Realty 3.27%, with HCL Technologies up 6.42% and TCS up 4.89%; Nifty Consumer Durables fell 1.33% and Nifty FMCG 0.94% (Liquide, Upstox).
Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,843 crore and domestic institutions ₹5,631 crore (Kotak Neo; provisional). The rupee closed at a provisional 92.44 per dollar, 24 paise weaker (PTI).

Brent settled at $96.57 a barrel, up 2.07%, after tankers reportedly hit mines near Hormuz and Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery; the 10-year G-Sec yield rose 7 basis points to 7.24%. IBJA's afternoon gold rate rose 1.32% to ₹1,22,641 per 10 g (The Nation, Business Standard, IBJA).
US stock markets were closed for Thanksgiving and trade a shortened session today; the DAX rose 2.08% and the Hang Seng 1.2% (Upstox, Dow Jones Newswires, AP).

drivers.title: Crude, the rupee and bonds
drivers.text: Brent settled at $96.57 on Thursday, up $1.96 or 2.07% (The Nation), after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit sea mines north of Oman's Khasab port and Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (Reuters via Euronext). The rupee closed at a provisional 92.44 per dollar (PTI), and the 10-year yield rose 7 basis points as dealers sold bonds on crude (Business Standard). Oil reaches India through the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign buying
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹1,27,945 crore of Indian shares from 1 to 26 November (Kotak Neo; provisional), and Business Upturn counted 18 sessions of net buying in a row. Foreign flows reach index heavyweights and the rupee.

drivers.title: US tariff proposal
drivers.text: The US Trade Representative's proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% with a trade deal (Business Standard), are open for public comment until 5 Jan 2027, with a hearing on 25 Jan 2027; India has rejected the excess-capacity finding (Business Today). Tariffs reach India through export-oriented sectors and the trade balance.

drivers.title: Rate expectations
drivers.text: The repo rate is 5.50% after a 25 basis point rise in October, and the next policy meeting runs from 2 to 4 Dec (RBI). Trading Economics reports growing expectations of a further 25 basis point rise on 4 Dec. Policy rates reach bank lending rates, deposit rates and bond yields.

drivers.title: Growth data
drivers.text: July to September GDP is due on Mon 30 Nov (MoSPI). A Business Standard compilation of 11 agencies' estimates has a median of 7.7%, in a range of 7.2% to 8.1%. Growth figures shape earnings estimates and feed into the RBI's decision.

global_cues.title: No US session overnight
global_cues.text: US stock markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen today for a session that ends early (Upstox News, citing the NYSE calendar). In Wednesday's session the S&P 500 fell 0.25% (Upstox News) after being down as much as 3.2% during the day (AP). US moves reach India through foreign flows and US-exposed sectors such as IT.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Thursday the Hang Seng rose 1.2%, the Nikkei 0.9% and the Kospi 0.3%, after the Kospi's 6.2% fall on Wednesday (AP). Early on Friday the Kospi was higher and the Nikkei little changed (JBizNews). Asia sets the regional tone for Indian trading.

global_cues.title: The dollar and US rates
global_cues.text: The dollar index held near 103.7 on Thursday (PTI, Newsquawk), and CME Group data showed a 98% chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December as of 24 Nov (Idéal Investisseur). US rates reach India through the dollar, the rupee and emerging-market flows.

global.headline: US stock markets were closed for Thanksgiving; Europe and Asia rose, with the DAX up 2.08% and the Hang Seng 1.2%
global.note: Closes are for Thursday 26 Nov. US stock markets were closed for Thanksgiving and close early today. AP gives Asian changes to one decimal, and the Shanghai Composite rose less than 0.1%. The FTSE 100's change is from its points change (PA rounds it to 1.8%); the DAX level is as reported, rounded to the point.

us.title: The holiday
us.text: US stock markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen on Friday for a shortened session that ends at 1 PM ET (Upstox News, citing the NYSE calendar; AP).

us.title: Wednesday's session
us.text: In the last full session the Dow rose 0.33% while the S&P 500 fell 0.25% and the Nasdaq Composite 0.6%; Nvidia fell 3.9% as AI shares weakened, and separately S&P Global Ratings warned it could cut the company's credit rating (AP, Upstox News).

us.title: Bonds and the dollar
us.text: The 10-year Treasury yield ended Wednesday at about 4.85%, according to Idéal Investisseur, citing US Treasury data, and the dollar index traded between 103.69 and 103.84 in thin holiday trading on Thursday (Newsquawk).

events.title: A December Fed rise priced in
events.text: US core PCE inflation was 3.3% and third-quarter growth was revised to 4.3% on Wednesday, and CME Group data on 24 Nov showed a 98% chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December (Idéal Investisseur). The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: ECB minutes
events.text: Minutes of the European Central Bank's October meeting showed many policymakers ready to raise rates, and futures price a 90% chance of a December rise (Investing.com). The channel to India: global rates and the dollar.

commentary.text: IBJA's Thursday morning rates were ₹1,22,982 per 10 g for gold and ₹1,46,933 per kg for silver, before GST and making charges.
Reuters reported spot gold up 0.3% in Asian trade on Thursday after it fell the day before to a 15-month low, briefly below $3,500 an ounce.

Reuters said the upward revision to US third-quarter growth and higher October inflation have traders expecting Fed rate rises next month and in early 2027; higher rates raise the cost of holding gold, which pays no interest.
Ilya Spivak of Tastylive said investors were covering short positions ahead of the US holiday (Reuters); USAGOLD noted that thin holiday trading can exaggerate price moves.

regulatory.text: Direct plans are now the default choice on fund houses' own websites and apps, and an investor who picks a regular plan is shown its higher expense ratio; regular plans remain available, including through distributors.
From 1 April 2027, a scheme may settle the cash for its outright cash-market purchases and sales on a net basis within the scheme; securities still settle trade by trade.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's scheme categories, as revised in February 2026 and summarised by Upstox, a multi asset allocation fund is a hybrid scheme that invests in at least three asset classes, such as equity, debt and gold or other commodities, with at least 10% in each. Because it holds assets that can move differently, its risk depends on how much it holds in each, and its value can still fall when share or commodity prices fall. Each scheme's riskometer level and risk factors are in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: Why fund assets can fall in a month when money flows in
paragraphs: A fund category's assets under management (AUM) change for two reasons: the money investors put in or take out (net flows), and the change in the market value of what the funds already hold, known as mark-to-market.

In October 2026, equity funds took in a net ₹32,994 crore, yet their assets fell 1.1% to ₹37.15 lakh crore; AMFI attributed the fall to mark-to-market losses (AMFI Monthly Note, October 2026). The fall in the value of holdings was larger than the new money that came in.

The reverse can also happen: assets can rise in a month of net outflows if prices rise enough. So a change in AUM does not on its own show whether investors added money, and AMFI's monthly note reports net flows and assets as separate figures.
